kind.odd: Three of these are kinds of {value}. Which one isn't?
kind.all: Tap all {n} weather phenomena that are kinds of {value}.

rows.label: nor'easter
rows.description: storm in the US and Canada
rows.hook: is a powerful winter storm that batters the Atlantic coast with heavy snow and howling winds

rows.label: tornado
rows.description: violently rotating column of air that is in contact with both the earth's surface and a cumulonimbus cloud in the air
rows.hook: is a violently spinning funnel of air that tears across land, famous from Kansas and The Wizard of Oz

rows.label: St. Elmo's fire
rows.description: weather phenomenon
rows.hook: is a glowing blue-white glow that sailors saw on the masts of ships during storms

rows.label: tropical cyclone
rows.description: rapidly rotating storm system that forms in the tropics
rows.hook: is a huge spinning storm over warm ocean waters, called a hurricane when it hits the Atlantic

rows.label: ball lightning
rows.description: extremely rare unexplained atmospheric electrical phenomenon
rows.hook: is a rarely seen, mysterious glowing sphere that floats in the air during storms

rows.label: rainbow
rows.description: meteorological phenomenon caused by reflection, refraction and dispersion of light in water droplets
rows.hook: is a colorful arc of red, orange, yellow, green, blue and violet that appears when sun shines through rain

rows.label: lightning
rows.description: weather phenomenon involving electrostatic discharge
rows.hook: is a giant spark of electricity in the sky, and Benjamin Franklin famously flew a kite in one

rows.label: typhoon
rows.description: mature tropical cyclone that forms in the Western North Pacific Ocean, with winds of at least 118 km/h (64 kts, 32.7 m/s)
rows.hook: is the name given to a powerful ocean storm when it strikes East Asia and the Pacific

rows.label: dew point
rows.description: temperature at which air becomes saturated with water vapour
rows.hook: is the temperature at which air becomes so damp that droplets start to form

rows.label: monsoon
rows.description: seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated with the asymmetric heating of land and sea
rows.hook: is a seasonal wind shift that brings months of heavy rain to South Asia

rows.label: sun dog
rows.description: atmospheric optical phenomenon
rows.hook: is a bright spot of light that appears beside the Sun, caused by ice crystals in the air

rows.label: derecho
rows.description: widespread, long-lived, straight-line wind storm associated with a land-based, fast-moving group of severe thunderstorms
rows.hook: is a fast-moving line of destructive straight-line winds that can flatten crops across the Midwest

rows.label: cloud
rows.description: visible mass of liquid droplets or frozen crystals suspended in the atmosphere
rows.hook: is a fluffy white or gray mass drifting in the sky, made of tiny droplets of water

rows.label: cumulonimbus
rows.description: genus of clouds, dense towering vertical cloud associated with thunderstorms and atmospheric instability
rows.hook: is the towering anvil-topped storm giant that brings thunder, hail and heavy rain

rows.label: humidity
rows.description: amount of water vapor in the air
rows.hook: is the amount of moisture in the air that makes a hot day feel sticky and muggy

rows.label: heat lightning
rows.description: lightning not accompanied by thunder sound
rows.hook: is the flashes seen on warm summer nights from a storm too far away to hear

rows.label: thunderstorm
rows.description: a storm characterized by the presence of lightning, usually accompanied by strong winds and often produce heavy rain and sometimes snow, sleet, or hail, but some produce little precipitation or no precipitation at all
rows.hook: is a stormy event with flashes, booms, gusty winds and heavy rain, often on hot afternoons

rows.label: waterspout
rows.description: weather phenomenon characterized by an intense columnar vortex that occurs over a body of water
rows.hook: is a spinning column of air and mist that rises from a lake or the sea

rows.label: rain
rows.description: liquid water in the form of droplets that have condensed from atmospheric water vapor and then precipitated
rows.hook: falls from the sky in drops, and is what umbrellas are made to keep off

rows.label: water cycle
rows.description: continuous movement of water on, above and below the surface of the Earth
rows.hook: is the endless loop in which rain evaporates from the seas, condenses and falls again

rows.label: contrail
rows.description: long, thin artificial clouds that sometimes form behind aircraft
rows.hook: is the white streak that a jet leaves across the sky at high altitude

rows.label: supercell
rows.description: thunderstorm that is characterized by the presence of a mesocyclone
rows.hook: is a long-lasting rotating storm that is the most dangerous kind, often spawning tornadoes

rows.label: jet stream
rows.description: fast-flowing atmospheric air-current
rows.hook: is a fast river of air high above the Earth that steers weather across continents and speeds up flights

rows.label: snow
rows.description: precipitation in the form of ice crystal flakes
rows.hook: falls as white flakes, and is what kids hope for to get a day off school

rows.label: trade wind
rows.description: permanent east-to-west prevailing winds that flow in the Earth's equatorial region
rows.hook: is a steady breeze that blows toward the equator and once carried sailing ships across the oceans

rows.label: precipitation
rows.description: liquid or solid water that falls to the ground
rows.hook: is the general term for rain, sleet, hail and snow falling from the sky

rows.label: thunder
rows.description: sound caused by a lightning strike
rows.hook: is the loud rumbling boom that follows a bright flash in the sky

rows.label: wind
rows.description: flow of gases or air on a large scale
rows.hook: is moving air that fills sails, spins turbines and blows kites

rows.label: halo
rows.description: optical phenomenon
rows.hook: is a bright ring of light seen around the Sun or Moon, caused by ice crystals
